clue.text: Initially, a measure direct from the source

parts.note: initially means at the start, the same as 'at first'
a hand is a measure of four inches, used for the height of horses

explanation.surface: Someone explains that, to begin with, a dose of something is drawn straight from where it originates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but here it is simply a synonym for the opening phrase of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Information obtained personally, without an intermediary, comes straight from its origin.

clue.text: Refraining from seeing Godiva in motion

indicators.note: something in motion is moving about, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone averts their eyes as Lady Godiva rides naked through Coventry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in motion' rearranges GODIVA plus IN; 'seeing' is only a link. Lady Godiva is the legendary noblewoman who rode naked through Coventry.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep from doing something is to shun or steer clear of it.

clue.text: Flounder, for example, in showy outfit

annotationWithheld.why: 'Flounder, for example, in showy outfit' (8): FLATFISH is FLASH (showy) round TFI, but TFI needs 'out' as an anagram indicator on 'fit' inside the single word 'outfit', one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Flounder, for example, in showy outfit

clue.text: Take one Asian coin up

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for 'take', on prescriptions
the Roman numeral I is one
the sen is a small coin of Japan and other Asian countries

explanation.surface: An instruction to pick up a piece of small change from somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is the definition in the sense of out of bed or above the horizon, as the sun is.
explanation.definitionFit: Having got out of bed or climbed above the horizon, someone or something has arisen.

clue.text: Polluted rain hit vanishing environment?

indicators.note: polluted water is fouled and spoilt, so these letters are corrupted into a new order

explanation.surface: Acid rain has damaged a natural habitat that is disappearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: things that vanish are said to disappear into this.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says a thing that disappears without trace has melted into the empty atmosphere.

clue.text: Germ-free — but in a month one gets cold!

parts.note: Sept is the short form of September
the Roman numeral I is one
C stands for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that even a sterile place lets a person catch a chill in a particular month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'gets' are links; the pieces run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sterile has been cleaned of all bacteria and other microbes.

clue.text: Talk that's loose is so crude

indicators.note: letters set loose are freed from their order, so these words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A complaint that conversation which is morally lax is also vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges IS SO CRUDE; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal speech or exchange on a subject is a lecture or conversation.

clue.text: Start to explode

definitions.meaning: to begin a journey, to depart
to cause a bomb or firework to go bang, to detonate

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to depart on a journey and to detonate a charge.

clue.text: Light shoe made of wood

definitions.meaning: an open summer shoe held on by straps
short for sandalwood, the fragrant timber of an Indian tree

explanation.surface: A description of flimsy footwear carved from timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a strappy open shoe and the scented timber also called sandalwood.

clue.text: Proceeded to delve into Tchaikovsky's first and last score

indicators.note: to delve into is to dig inside, so one piece goes within the other
the first and last letters of the composer's name are taken

parts.note: proceeded means moved on, or went

explanation.surface: A musician sets about studying the opening and closing pages of a Tchaikovsky score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like sheet music, but it is the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is an old word for a group of twenty, as in 'three score years and ten'.

clue.text: Second-in-command needs friends — they're precious

indicators.note: the second letter in the following word is taken

parts.note: pals are friends

explanation.surface: A deputy officer is said to need companions, who are valued highly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second-in-command' reads as a deputy, but it means the second letter in 'command'.
explanation.definitionFit: These iridescent gemstones are semi-precious stones prized in jewellery.

clue.text: Fashionable fragrance, fundamentally

parts.note: something in fashion is said to be 'in'
an essence is a concentrated perfume

explanation.surface: A trendy perfume is described as basically what it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Basically, at heart, by its very nature: the phrase means in its essential qualities.

clue.text: Object to article held by skilful one in court

indicators.note: something held by another sits inside its grip

parts.note: deft means skilful
an end is an object or aim
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A lawyer protests against a clause put forward by a clever opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb meaning protest, but it is a noun meaning purpose. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The accused person in a trial is the party standing in the dock.

clue.text: Some tucked behind back of piano — forte of Bridget Riley

indicators.note: one piece is placed after the other, tucked in behind it
the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: part means some, a portion

explanation.surface: Someone hides papers behind a piano, a speciality of the painter Bridget Riley.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridget Riley is a British painter famous for dizzying black-and-white abstracts.
explanation.definitionFit: Riley is the best-known exponent of this 1960s style of optical-illusion abstract painting.

clue.text: Retsina, when drunk, is not so nice

indicators.note: a drunk person reels about, so these letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A verdict that the Greek resinated wine tastes worse once you have drunk it.
explanation.walkthrough: Retsina is a Greek wine flavoured with pine resin. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of an adjective meaning unpleasant: more disagreeable.

clue.text: Camping upset no-one? That's the aim

parts.note: someone camping is sleeping under canvas

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run upward

parts.note: NO plus I, one as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone sleeping outdoors hopes nobody is disturbed and states the purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no-one' looks like nobody but splits into NO and I (one); 'upset' turns that into ION. 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A purpose or plan is what someone means to achieve.

clue.text: Fish, beef or grouse?

definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish of ponds and rivers

explanation.surface: A question about what is on the menu: fish, red meat or game bird?
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a freshwater fish and, as a verb, means to find fault and complain.

clue.text: Ear-piercing fish in southern river

indicators.note: one piece sits inside another

parts.note: the Trent is a river in the English Midlands
the ide or id is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A deafening fish is found in a river in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is a major river of the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill, loud and grating sound hurts the ears.

clue.text: Coin put in trust not long ago

indicators.note: one piece is put inside another

parts.note: to rely on is to trust
a cent is a coin

explanation.surface: Someone says money was placed in a trust fund only lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trust' looks like a fund, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Lately, a short time back, in the near past.

clue.text: Supporter backing New York baseball team

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the team's name is read from the end

parts.note: the Mets are a New York baseball team

explanation.surface: A fan cheers for a New York side in America's pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan, but it is the part of a plant that holds up the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant's stalk holds up its leaves and flowers.

clue.text: French linesman: "I got man sent off"

indicators.note: sent off suggests something dispatched and disordered, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French football official says he dismissed a player.
explanation.walkthrough: André Maginot was the French war minister after whom the Maginot Line of defences was named.
explanation.definitionFit: The French minister gave his name to a fortified line along the eastern border.

clue.text: Speak softly and be heartbroken

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone is told to whisper and be devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartbroken' reads as one word, but 'broken' rearranges BE plus HEART. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe words is to whisper or utter them very quietly.

clue.text: Reportedly what shopaholics do eventually

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the following words are heard rather than read

parts.note: shopaholics buy and buy

explanation.surface: Someone notes how compulsive shoppers behave in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in due course, after a while.

clue.text: Film about unknown Conservative leader, terribly posh

indicators.note: one piece goes around another
terribly suggests badly done, so these letters are mangled

parts.note: Y is an unknown in algebra

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A documentary about an anonymous Tory leader with an awfully upper-class manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges POSH into PS...HO, which goes 'about' Y and C. PSYCHO is Hitchcock's 1960 thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock's 1960 thriller about Norman Bates is a famous movie.

clue.text: Check polish again

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
to buff is to polish

explanation.surface: Someone inspects their shoes, then shines them a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like inspect, but it means repel.
explanation.definitionFit: To check an advance is to repulse or snub it.

clue.text: Beer mug for Gertrude

definitions.meaning: a large earthenware tankard for beer
Gertrude ..., the American writer living in Paris

explanation.surface: A tankard is chosen for a woman called Gertrude.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a German-style beer tankard and the surname of the American writer Gertrude.

clue.text: Plant an intelligence network

definitions.meaning: a climbing plant that bears bunches of fruit for wine
an informal route by which gossip and rumour spread

explanation.surface: Instructions to plant a spy ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the fruit-bearing climber and the informal network for rumour, as in 'heard it on the ...'.

clue.text: A bird you may see down under

definitions.text: A bird you may see down under

parts.words: A bird you may see down under
parts.note: reads as an Australian bird, but means a duck whose name comes before the word 'down', so it precedes it

explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' suggests Australia, but this sea duck's soft feathers fill quilts, and its name is followed by 'down' in the compound word.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea duck whose soft breast feathers are used to fill quilts.

clue.text: Warned about education

indicators.note: about suggests moving round, so these letters are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A teacher was told off about schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it rearranges EDUCATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone given a warning has been told to take care.

clue.text: Lived in the past — that is to escape from the German world

indicators.note: something that escapes from another is removed from it

parts.note: German for 'the world' is die Welt

explanation.surface: A nostalgic person dwells on history; that is, they want to flee from Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lived in the past' is the whole definition: a past tense of 'live'.
explanation.definitionFit: Resided or stayed, a past tense of the verb meaning to make one's home.

clue.text: See 7
Basic details, pretty rhymes

parts.note: both halves of the phrase rhyme with the word 'pretty'

explanation.surface: Fundamental facts are dressed up in sweet-sounding verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a rhyming compound, each half rhyming with 'pretty'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the essential practical facts of a matter.
